author: claude-code-session-2026-08-28
evidence: D0026 (2026-08-26): tools/layer_lint/no_engine_imports.py checked engine coupling against a hand-picked class-name list, accumulated one class at a time as someone tripped on a missing one (D0023). An audit against Godot's actual ClassDB registry found 282 Node-derived classes against the four stems the list actually covered -- 276 more classes the gate would have silently let through. Fixed by deriving the list mechanically from the engine's own registry instead of accumulating it by hand.

D0091 (2026-08-27): two of the project's own run-language sweeps (D0082's docs/GDD.md-only grep pass, and a reversal commit's queue-named file list) both missed CLAUDE.md, docs/CLAIMS.md, eight sim/*/MODULE.md files, and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §5/§6's own worked example -- found in one pass by an independent external audit reading the corpus cold, with no model of which files 'should' need checking (docs/DECISIONS_LEDGER.md D0087 names the eight MODULE.md fixes this produced). D0091 itself named the general law in prose, citing D0026 as the first instance and this as the second.

D0075 (2026-08-27): tools/anvil/test_check_integrity.py's own mutation-test fixtures, written specifically to test the referential-integrity checker's correctness, both self-referenced (a MEASUREMENT event naming itself as its own claim_id) without the fixture author noticing -- because the space of cases the fixtures were modeling, at the time they were written, did not include self-reference as a candidate. Invisible until D0069's typed-reference check landed and broke both fixtures independently. The same law, one level more abstract: the 'corpus' being swept was the space of validation cases a test suite's own author had modeled, not a set of files, but the shape (a check's own coverage bounded by what its author thought to include) is identical.

D0102 (2026-08-28, this session): tools/quality_check/scan.py's own find_gd_files() -- inside the exact instrument this whole failure class motivated building -- was scoped to a fixed GAME_DIRS list (core/sim/interface/view/shell), missing tests/ (and data/*/generated.gd) entirely, for four full rounds (D0096-D0101). duplication.py reported '0 clusters' every one of those rounds while never having scanned roughly two-thirds of the tree's own .gd files. Found running a full-tree sweep for the first time, not by an external cold reader this time but by checking the scanner's own docstring claim ('same scope check_size_limits.py uses') against check_size_limits.py's actual behavior -- a narrower, cheaper correction method than a full independent audit, worth naming as a partial methodological improvement even though the underlying failure shape is identical to the prior three.
narrative: Severity high, not medium: this is not a single incident but a confirmed-recurring class with four independent instances across three sessions, one of which happened inside the very instrument suite built to catch exactly this shape of gap -- if the quality-instrument suite itself is not immune, no future sweep in this project should be trusted at face value without asking what it was modeled to cover. Practical consequence, stated for the next audit rather than left implicit: prefer a corpus-wide mechanical check (or a comparison against an independently-scoped peer scanner, as D0102's fix used) over an enumerated list of 'the files/classes/cases this probably needs to cover' whenever completeness matters -- the enumeration IS the boundary that goes on to miss things. This event does not invalidate any prior CLAIM_AUTHORED or ASSUMPTION; it names a pattern across FINDINGS and DECISIONS, which the schema's own invalidates field cannot reference directly (independent_of and invalidates both take source-class/event lists respectively, neither is the right field for citing prior FINDINGS as evidence, which is why the citations live in the evidence list instead).
observation: A sweep bounded by its author's own model of the corpus cannot see what is outside that model, and a green result from such a sweep is evidence only about the covered subset -- named once already in ledger prose (docs/DECISIONS_LEDGER.md D0091) with two instances, now confirmed a recurring, reliable failure class with two more independent instances since, one inside this project's own quality-instrument suite. Filed as one durable Anvil event, consolidating what was five scattered ledger notes across three sessions, so a future audit has one thing to check the project against rather than needing to already know to go looking for the pattern.
